ops-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency breach on runtime-us-east-1 — model-streamer-prod. Page: oncall
Aisha: acked. pinging Ben (primary oncall)
Ben: I'm oncall, pulling graphs now. p95 ~420ms, p99 spiking to 3.2s over last 6m. streaming stalls increasing.
Ben: quick scrape of runtime metrics:
```
/admin/cache/stats
kv_items: 1.23M
kv_capacity: 1.50M
cache_evictions/sec: 472
prefill_rate_rps: 130
decode_rate_rps: 540
kv_fragmentation_ratio: 0.78
avg_kv_lookup_ms: 7.1
```
Ben: looks like KV cache pressure + fragmentation. eviction churn high, prefill workers not keeping up with decode. tail latency coming from cache misses and backed up decode queue.
Kevin: tagging in — recent deploy that changed prefill_batch_size to 32?
Ben: yep that was the canary from last deploy 22:10 UTC. suspect prefill throughput dropped.
Ravi: streaming stall traces show long waits in kv_lookup and then retrying decode, causing head-of-line delays.
Aisha: customer impact? any 5xxs or client visible errors?
Ben: no increased 5xxs so far, but streaming stalls affect p99 token latency and some long-tail slow clients. estimated 4-6% of requests with token delay >2s in last 10m.
Carmen: ack, I'll coordinate external comms if that climbs >10%
Ben: mitigation plan in next 5m:
- revert prefill_batch_size to 64 for canary pods
- scale prefill-worker deployment +2 replicas
- if that fails, route small fraction (10%) of traffic to model-variant-lite which bypasses KV cache
Executing now.
```
# scale prefill workers
kubectl scale deploy/prefill-worker -n prod --replicas=6
# patch canary to revert batch size
kubectl set env deploy/runtime-canary -n prod PREFILL_BATCH_SIZE=64
```
Ben: scaled prefill -> replicas=6 (ok). patched runtime-canary env. watching metrics.
(2m)
Ben: prefill_rate up to 320 rps, cache_evictions/sec dropping to 210, p99 trending down to ~980ms
Aisha: nice. Any need to route traffic off main variant?
Ben: not yet. continuing to watch for stabilization. leaving canary patch for 10m then roll to rest.
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] Sev3 created: INC-20260314-0036 — latency spike, assigned to Ben
Ravi: I recommend increasing KV_MAX_ITEMS on the node group to 1.8M as a medium-term fix to reduce churn; will prepare a change.
Ben: agreed. I'll also add a quick cache compaction job to defragment shards later tonight.
Carmen: taking the next shift at +45m. handoff notes:
- primary cause: prefill vs decode imbalance after canary changed PREFILL_BATCH_SIZE
- current mitigation: reverted batch size on canary, scaled prefill-workers
- impact: ~4% requests with token latency >2s at peak, now dropping
- next steps: monitor for 30m, roll canary patch to fleet if stable, schedule KV capacity increase
Carmen: assigning follow-up ticket SIG-1257 to infra for KV capacity and compaction
Ben: thanks, handing off to Carmen. I'll be reachable if it flares
Aisha: thanks all — CS notified with current impact numbers and mitigation steps
Ben: final check 30m later: p95 360ms p99 680ms cache_evictions/sec ~45 prefill_rate 480 rps
Carmen: I'll keep an eye overnight. if p99 creeps back over 1.5s I will trigger fallback routing to variant-lite
ops-bot: [RESOLVED] incident INC-20260314-0036 marked resolved after metrics stabilized and mitigations applied
Aisha: short postmortem please, include prefill batch size as regression candidate and add an alert for prefill_rate/decouple ratio
Carmen: will draft a short postmortem tomorrow morning and link to SIG-1257
Ben: adding logs + commands run to the ticket for ops runbook
Ravi: noted. marking done from infra side for immediate actions
ops-bot: incident thread auto-archived
